icons.basis: Photoshop's slanted brush and Procreate's brush tip — handle up-right, tip down-left.
icons.note: Handle, ferrule, solid tapered head.

icons.basis: The Photoshop and Illustrator pencil: a sharpened shaft on the same diagonal.
icons.note: Shaft, collar, sharpened cone with a solid graphite point.

icons.basis: Photoshop's airbrush option — a nozzle throwing a widening cone.
icons.note: Canister, cone of air, one landed particle.

icons.basis: Procreate's inking and marker brush families — a fat barrel cut to a chisel.
icons.note: Fat banded barrel, cut off at a solid chisel wedge.

icons.basis: Procreate's technical pen and Photoshop's ink brushes — a split dip-pen nib.
icons.note: Pointed nib, split down the middle, solid at the point.

icons.basis: Illustrator's calligraphic brush — a flat edge held at a fixed angle to the stroke.
icons.note: Slim holder and a solid broad edge canted off the axis.

icons.basis: Procreate's Artistic set — the wrapped wax stub.
icons.note: Short barrel with wrapper bands, worn to a blunt solid nose.

icons.basis: Procreate's chalk and soft-pastel brushes — a square stick that sheds.
icons.note: Square stick, blunt at the solid end, shedding dust.

icons.basis: Procreate's charcoal brushes — a broken stick, never a manufactured one.
icons.note: Irregular chunk, solid where it has been worn flat.

icons.basis: Procreate's Wet Media — a soft round loaded over a spreading pool.
icons.note: Round brush above the water it has already put down.

icons.basis: Photoshop's bristle-tip brushes — the only tool that shows its hairs.
icons.note: Flat ferrule with splayed bristles.

icons.basis: Illustrator's Blob Brush — a brush whose strokes fuse into one filled shape.
icons.note: A brush laying down a closed form rather than a line.

icons.basis: Procreate's Spraypaints set, and the app's own mural heritage.
icons.note: Rattle can, nozzle out the side, one landed burst.

icons.basis: Procreate's roller brushes — sleeve, cranked stem, grip.
icons.note: Roller and handle, with one drip already laid down.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Clone Stamp — the rubber stamp, unchanged since 1990.
icons.note: Knob, plate, and the solid face that transfers the sample.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Pattern Stamp — the same stamp, printing a tile instead of a sample.
icons.note: Stamp over a chequer.

icons.basis: The Photoshop and Procreate block eraser — held flat, not angled like a brush.
icons.note: A rubber block, banded, solid at the face doing the wiping.

icons.basis: Photoshop's hard round eraser preset.
icons.note: The block against an unbroken rule — the edge stays where it is put.

icons.basis: Photoshop's soft round eraser preset.
icons.note: The same block against a broken rule — the edge dissolves.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Smudge and Procreate's Smudge — a fingertip dragging wet pigment.
icons.note: A solid pad pulled out into three trailing lines.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Blur tool — the water drop, unchanged.
icons.note: The drop, with the detail under it collapsing into bands.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Sharpen tool — the sharpening cone next to the blur drop.
icons.note: The cone, solid at the tip that does the work.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Dodge tool — the darkroom paddle on its wire, throwing light back.
icons.note: Paddle, rod, and the light it holds off the paper.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Burn tool — the hand cupped into an aperture to concentrate exposure.
icons.note: A cupped C with the light it funnels burning solid at the centre.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Sponge tool — a porous block that pulls colour out or drives it in.
icons.note: Pores, one of them filled where the colour is being taken.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Healing Brush — the sticking plaster, on the tool diagonal.
icons.note: A plaster with the sampled centre solid.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Spot Healing Brush — the plaster reduced to the spot it targets.
icons.note: A ring sighted on a single blemish.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Patch tool — a drawn region dragged onto clean ground.
icons.note: A hand-drawn area moved to a rectangle of good surface.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Red Eye tool — an eye reduced to lid, iris and pupil.
icons.note: The one solid pupil being corrected.

icons.basis: Procreate's Liquify and Photoshop's Twirl — the surface pulled into a spiral.
icons.note: Three turns tightening on the point being pushed.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Paint Bucket and Illustrator's Live Paint — the tipped can.
icons.note: A tipped bucket, with the drop that has already left it.

icons.basis: The Photoshop and Illustrator eyedropper — bulb, barrel, point.
icons.note: The dropper, solid where it takes the sample.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Mixer Brush — a loaded brush over the swirl it stirs.
icons.note: A brush working colour already on the surface.

icons.basis: Procreate's Brush Library — a set of loaded brushes rather than one.
icons.note: A pot of brushes, each with paint on it.

icons.basis: Procreate's Brush Studio and Photoshop's Brush Settings — stacked parameter rails.

icons.basis: Photoshop's brush-size preview — nested footprints on one centre.
icons.note: Two diameters measured out from a single origin.

icons.basis: Procreate's opacity slider thumb — one disc half laid down.
icons.note: Half committed, half withheld.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Flow control — how much arrives per pass, not how dark it ends up.
icons.note: Three drops at three depths of fall.

icons.basis: Photoshop's hardness preview — solid core, soft shoulder, outer limit.
icons.note: A solid core, a broken halo, an outer edge.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Spacing setting — a brush is a run of stamps, not a line.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Scattering — marks thrown off the path they were meant to follow.
icons.note: A stroke path with its stamps scattered around it.

icons.basis: Photoshop's brush Angle dial and Illustrator's calligraphic angle.
icons.note: An angle read off the baseline, solid where it points.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Roundness control — a round footprint compressed on one axis.
icons.note: A circle squeezed against its own limit.

icons.basis: Photoshop's jitter controls — a value that refuses to hold still.
icons.note: A wandering parameter above a fixed baseline.

icons.basis: Procreate's Taper settings — a stroke that opens, swells and closes.
icons.note: One stroke, thin at both ends.

icons.basis: Procreate's Wet Mix — two loads bleeding into each other.
icons.note: Two footprints overlapping; the wet edge is where they meet.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Build-up airbrush behaviour — passes stacking over one another.
icons.note: Three passes over the same ground.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Dual Brush — a second tip riding inside the first.
icons.note: A smaller footprint carried by a larger one.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Texture setting and Procreate's grain source — paper tooth as a field.

icons.basis: Procreate's brush import and Photoshop's .abr load.

icons.basis: Procreate's stylus settings — the barrel and the tip the digitiser reads.

icons.basis: Procreate's Pressure curve — force registered at the point of contact.

icons.basis: Procreate's Tilt settings — the lean of the barrel against the surface.
icons.note: An angle measured off the plane the tool rests on.

icons.basis: Procreate's StreamLine — the same gesture above and below the filter.

icons.basis: Procreate's QuickShape — a hand-drawn loop pulled onto true geometry.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Rectangular Marquee — ants, with one corner handle live.

icons.basis: Photoshop's Elliptical Marquee.
